issue_records.title: Runic breaks unpacking of only the first element of a tuple
issue_records.body_excerpt:
```julia
julia> Runic.format_string("x, = (1, 2, 3)")
"x = (1, 2, 3)"
```
That is, of course, not equivalent:
```julia
julia> x, = (1, 2, 3); x
1

julia> x = (1, 2, 3); x
(1, 2, 3)
```

defect_evidence_basis.assessment: Issue demonstrates that formatting changes tuple destructuring semantics; the single-parent fixing commit directly closes the issue.

issue_records.title: Fix trailing comma in implicit tuples in destructuring
issue_records.body_excerpt: This patch fixes the usage of trailing commas in implicit tuples when used in destructuring assignment, e.g. `x, = z`. In this context the trailing comma is needed to preserve the tuple node, which is different from e.g. implicit tuples in `do`-blocks. A trailing comma is allowed (e.g. preserved from the source) for multi-item implicit tuples so that e.g. `x, y, = z` can be used to signal that z contains more than two items. Closes #58.

Fix trailing comma in implicit tuples in destructuring (#59)

This patch fixes the usage of trailing commas in implicit tuples when
used in destructuring assignment, e.g. `x, = z`. In this context the
trailing comma is needed to preserve the tuple node, which is different
from e.g. implicit tuples in `do`-blocks. A trailing comma is allowed
(e.g. preserved from the source) for multi-item implicit tuples so that
e.g. `x, y, = z` can be used to signal that z contains more than two
items. Closes #58.
